correctness.rationale: Explicit two-case proof: choose nonscalar source A0, its centralizer span{I,A0}; if all source matrices commute, their affine form reduces the full family to A0 and an exact two-dimensional single-pair bound. Otherwise the joint commutant is scalars, a nonzero product of inverse-amplification blocks forces an invertible common intertwiner, and every amplified common intertwiner is C⊗X with multiplicative condition number. The single-pair optimum follows from rank-one nilpotent and normalized involution unitary canonical forms; the usual two-sided norm ratio is a lower bound at all amplification sizes. Scalar and nonsimilar boundaries treated. Standalone checker finite 79 assertions, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Resolves the sharp constant for the first nontrivial matrix size in the natural arbitrary-family simultaneous similarity-cancellation question explicitly posed with an unknown uniform C(n,q,t) by Aouichaoui. The result is an all-index-set quantitative classification and sharp no-gain under replication, with a structural difference between commuting one-generator and noncommuting scalar-commutant regimes. It is not merely a fixed arbitrary numeric example or a new name for the already-known single-pair case.
